q: How much of the whole-genome BLASTN identity shift we observed (98.26% for LU2 vs KCTC 2190 vs the paper's reported 99.44%) is aligner-choice artefact vs a real underestimate?
basis: Our replication used blastn with -perc_identity 70 (inclusive of lower-identity HSPs), while the paper cited web BLAST identities. Mash on the same genome pair reports ~98.61% ANI-equivalent, closer to our BLAST number than to the paper's. This is a methodology-vs-truth gap that a systematic aligner comparison could close.
next_steps: Run pyani (ANIm and ANIb) and FastANI on the same 8-reference set (CP035466 + the 8 references cited in the paper). Compare the three aligners' whole-genome ANI values and check whether any of them recovers ~99.44%. If none do, contact the corresponding author for the exact BLAST parameters used, or treat the paper's identity numbers as web-BLAST-tool-specific and re-annotate all comparative-genomics work in the paper accordingly.

q: Are the intrinsic oqxAB (quinolone), fosA (fosfomycin) and uhpT-E350Q (fosfomycin) resistance signatures that AMRFinderPlus 2024-07-22.1 flags in LU2 — but that Szczerba et al. did not report from ResFinder 3.1 in 2020 — phenotypically active?
basis: AMRFinderPlus surfaces 11 AMR/virulence loci in LU2 (including chromosomal quinolone efflux oqxAB, fosA5, and the uhpT E350Q fosfomycin-resistance point mutation) that are not in the paper's Table 2. These have direct biotechnology implications: LU2 is being proposed as an industrial succinic-acid platform, and industrial permits typically require an AMR-free chassis. The DB delta between 2020 ResFinder 3.1 and 2024 AMRFinderPlus is real, but silent-DNA presence does not equal phenotypic resistance.
next_steps: Run MIC assays on LU2 for ciprofloxacin (tests oqxAB function) and fosfomycin (tests fosA/uhpT) using CLSI protocols. If LU2 is resistant, it may be unsuitable for GRAS/QPS classification for industrial use; if susceptible, the intrinsic loci are cryptic or unexpressed. Also cross-check by running ResFinder 4.x (current version) against LU2 to see whether the delta is DB-only or DB+tool.

q: Does LU2 actually produce succinate through the reductive-TCA + glyoxylate route the paper infers from gene presence, or is that inference contradicted by carbon-flux measurements on whey permeate?
basis: We independently confirmed that every gene in the paper's proposed route (ppc, mdh, fumABC/D, frdABCD, aceA, aceB, pykF, ppsA) is present in the CP035466.1 annotation. But gene presence ≠ flux. The paper never measured actual carbon flux — the succinate biosynthesis pathway is entirely inferred. On whey permeate specifically (LU2's paper substrate), catabolite repression from lactose metabolism could easily reroute flux away from the reductive TCA branch.
next_steps: Perform ¹³C-metabolic flux analysis (¹³C-MFA) on LU2 grown on U-¹³C-lactose whey permeate, quantifying labelling patterns in succinate, malate, and citrate. If the reductive branch is dominant, the paper's mechanistic claim is supported; if the TCA runs oxidatively and succinate comes from a different route (e.g. propionate-degradation-adjacent pathways given the rumen origin), the paper's model needs revision.

q: Has the ~4× growth of PHASTER's reference phage database since 2019 changed the identity, boundaries, or count of intact prophages detectable in LU2?
basis: The paper's PHASTER run in 2019 identified one intact prophage of ~31.9 kb best-matching Salmonella phage RE-2010 (HM770079). We did not rerun PHASTER (web-only, rate-limited) but did confirm 8 prophage-machinery genes (integrase, tail, tape-measure) in the annotation. Since 2019, PHASTER's phage DB has grown substantially and many Enterobacter-specific phages have been sequenced.
next_steps: Rerun PHASTER (or the newer PHASTEST) on CP035466.1 in 2026, and compare intact-region count, boundaries, and best-hit reference vs the paper. Also run VirSorter2 and geNomad as prokaryotic-viral second opinions. Any change in prophage boundaries would materially affect the paper's HGT/mobilome burden analysis (which used the 2019 PHASTER call as a foundational input).

q: Given that LU2 has no CRISPR/Cas system, one intact prophage, 47 genomic islands, and many IS/tandem repeats, is its mobilome burden actually elevated compared to the KCTC 2190 reference — as the rumen ecology hypothesis would predict — or is it typical for the K. aerogenes species?
basis: The paper reports mobile-element counts for LU2 alone but never runs the same IslandViewer 4 + PHASTER + IS-finder pipeline on KCTC 2190 or the 22 other K. aerogenes genomes it compares against in Table 1. Without a species-level baseline it's impossible to say whether LU2's mobilome is enriched or ordinary. A rumen-adapted strain should plausibly show elevated HGT signatures.
next_steps: Run identical IslandViewer 4, PHASTER, and ISEScan pipelines on all 22 complete K. aerogenes genomes available at NCBI (as of 2026, likely 40+). Compute GI count / IS count / prophage burden per Mb, and test whether LU2 is a mobilome-burden outlier using a Grubbs or MAD-based outlier test. Correlate with each strain's ecological source (clinical, environmental, rumen) to test the rumen-HGT-enrichment hypothesis rigorously.
